name: Rene Dubois

Hopping strategically between the two sides of the law, he is frequently found robbing art pieces from remote galleries as he is assisting in their retrieval. With a skill set derived from his criminal activities, Rene is skilled in climbing, stealth and acrobatics, and is multilingual, speaking French, Spanish, Basque and English.In-game agent dossier, James Bond: World of Espionage. Rene was assigned to assist James Bond by his niece Justine and rescues him by boat from Ludovic de Baleine's assassin Dragomir. name: Anaelle Brouchard
text_excerpt: Anaelle Brouchard is a fictional French cryptographer who is associated with Dauphin Baleine. The character appeared in the 2015 video-game James Bond: World of Espionage, during its Slow Down Faster story-line. Game biography Despite her reputation as a naïve and optimistic girl, Anaelle pursued studies in cryptography and computer science, As she further descended into the world of the 'ark net' she began to live a complex life, with multiple online identities who no one could trace back to her. In-game agent dossier, James Bond: World of Espionage. James Bond first encounters Brouchard after his initial contact in the Alps, Justine Dubois, points him in her direction believing that she is in possession of a key which he is searching for. The pair dine together, during which it is revealed that her key was given the key by her jealous 'friend', Ludovic de Baleine. Later Baleine's henchman Dragomir wounds 007 and he encounters Anaelle in the chalet which the Dauphin bought for her.

Ultimately, Charnage's incompetence led to a boy called James Bond taking the machine's designer Alexis Fairburn being rescued from them. Sedova then had Charnage killed by his own mercenary henchman, Ludwig Smith, and went to take Fairburn back, and ended up with Perry Mandeville as an additional hostage as she and one of her lieutenants dragged Fairburn through London's abandoned Pneumatic Rail System tunnels. She eventually dropped Mandeville after hitting him with her gun, and eventually became aware of Bond's presence. Nevertheless, she is a child at heart and her schoolgirl fantasies of love and romance make her susceptible to persuasion and a liability to the FSB. name: Alexander Sechenov
text_excerpt: Alexander Sechenov (Russian: Александр Сеченов) is a fictional MI6 mole within the FSB of Russia. The character appeared in the 2015 video-game James Bond: World of Espionage, during its From Russia with Love story-line. Game biography After years of complex interaction with the authorities, the paranoid Alexander Sechenov was finally turned in a video game chatroom to use his skills to assist MI6 in the capture of a Chechen terrorist. Despite his unsavoury habits, MI6 deemed him useful enough to keep out of Russian prison and has been utilizing him as a mole within the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation (FSB).In-game agent dossier, James Bond: World of Espionage. During the early missions of the From Russia with Love story-line 007 meets with Sechenov to confirm the authenticity of a mysterious hash key he had obtained. name: Oliver Arsenault
text_excerpt: Oliver Arsenault is a fictional arms dealer who appeared in the 2015 video-game James Bond: World of Espionage, during its Spectre Part 1 story-line. Biography With the address of Marco Sciarra's rendezvous with Gallo in his possession, James Bond meets with arms dealer Oliver Arsenault in a Mexican back alley to procure a sniper rifle for the job. name: Luiz Quinonez
text_excerpt: Luiz Quinonez is a Mexican intelligence operative working with the American CIA. The character appeared in the 2015 video-game James Bond: World of Espionage, during its Spectre Part 1 story-line. Biography After arriving in Mexico, James Bond liaises with old CIA friend Felix Leiter, who takes the spy to meet his local colleague, Luiz Quinonez. Quinonez has been investigating the address which was of interest to terrorist and SPECTRE operative, Marco Sciarra. The building was a block of apartments, mainly for discrete, short-term rentals. Apartment 6 was recently rented by Gallo, a cartel smuggler known for moving narcotics and explosives across the American/Mexican border. While briefly included in the main story of the game, the character was not actually a collectable 'agent'. Mr. DNA was created by InGen to help visitors understand the processes involved in the creation of the dinosaurs on Jurassic Park. A film starring him and InGen's founder John Hammond would be played in a theater located in the park's Visitor Center before a tour. Mr. DNA also was used on the maintenance board of Jurassic Park's Geothermal Power Plant and on a board telling how tall a person must be to ride the upcoming Bone Shaker roller coaster. After the Jurassic Park Incident the cartoon character seemed to have been put out of service by his company for about a decade.
